newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO PESO ENDS STRONG ON BOURSE, MKT AWAITS DATA.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO PESO ENDS STRONG ON BOURSE, MKT AWAITS DATA.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer across the board on Tuesday on capital flows to the local bourse in what traders said was a cautious session.
"The market is awaiting U.S. economic data later this week and possible spillover. We just went through the motions today, the real movement will come tomorrow," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.0 and 1.85 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7840/7.7870 and 7.7795/7.7825 per dollar.
The local bourse's leading IPC index was up 0.28 percent at 5,057.69 points when foreign exchange trading closed.
Dealers said they would closely watch reaction on the U.S. bond market to U.S. retail sales data on Wednesday, and inflation data on Thursday.
The peso also gained strength due to dealers switching out of dollars in order to participate in the central bank auction later in the day, dealers said.
A Reuters survey of nine money market dealers showed they forecast an average rise of 44 basis points to 18.79 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates.

Traders also noted that players chose not to exercise dollar put options despite the strength of the peso. They estimated $142 million in puts had yet to be exercised, out of $500 million auctioned by the central bank on July 31.
